newsitem.title: LATVIA: OGRE FORESTRY SAYS BACK IN PROFIT JAN, FEB 97.
newsitem.headline: OGRE FORESTRY SAYS BACK IN PROFIT JAN, FEB 97.

text.p: Timber company Ogre Forestry said on Thursday it was back in profit in January and February of 1997 versus the same period of 1996 and saw more hope if the current pulpwood prices and dollar rate persisted.
"Given that the current pulpwood prices and dollar exchange rate will continue, there is a glimmer of hope," Imants Ansons, Ogre president, told Reuters in an interview.
"$33 dollars for a cubic metre of coniferous pulp wood and $27 dollars for birch is quite satisfactory," he added.
Ogre had a 7,347 lats profit before tax in the first two months of this year against a loss of 17,357 lats before tax in January and February of 1996, Ansons said.
Ogre, a secondary list share on the Riga bourse, earlier reported a loss of 58,759 lats in 1996 on net turnover of 475,801 lats. Its fixed assets were 166,147 lats.
Out of some 45,000 cubic metres of timber produced last year some 10,000 cubic metres were sold as pulpwood and about 20,000 tonnes as sawmill timber.
The rest was sold as fire-wood on the local market.
Ogre expected to increase its total volume this year, Ansons said, but declined to be specific.
